topic: How does the preamble structure with concatenated ZC sequences impact link budget calculations for GEO satellite coverage?
consensus_response: The preamble structure with concatenated Zero-Correlation (ZC) sequences in GEO satellite systems significantly impacts link budget calculations due to the long propagation delay (~540 ms). This causes increased interference and reduced signal-to-interference ratio (SIR), affecting detection performance. The array factor mismatch due to Doppler Shift leads to a reduced correlation peak amplitude, increasing the noise floor and decreasing the detection probability. To mitigate this, advanced synchronization techniques can be employed, but at the cost of added system complexity. Moreover, Atmospheric Attenuation effects on concatenated ZC sequences also impact signal strength and phase, necessitating adaptive modulation techniques to mitigate attenuation effects.
